Question B-006-002-011.

Why the correct answer is right: Open-wire line has two conductors held side by side at a fixed spacing by insulating spreaders. That construction leaves mostly air between and around the wires.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "Coaxial cable": Coaxial conductors are arranged one inside the other and are separated by dielectric, not by side-by-side spreaders.
- sourceIndex 2: "Twin-lead": Twin-lead keeps its two conductors in a flat plastic strip, so spreaders are not the feature being described.
- sourceIndex 3: "Twisted pair": Twisted-pair conductors repeatedly change position around each other instead of staying side by side a constant distance apart.
